domain: water resources / national dam-storage daily panel
prediction_question: For a Mexican dam in the CONAGUA SIH reservoir network (210 catalogued dams, 26 states) whose published stored volume VolumenAlm on the latest available day T is at or above the drought threshold (25 percent of the dam's reference capacity), will VolumenAlm fall below that threshold on at least one day in the 30 calendar days after T (a drought-onset event)? A useful prediction supports water-allocation planning, drought-monitoring inputs (the official Monitor de Sequia en Mexico uses reservoir availability as an index), and urban supply outlooks (Monterrey 2022, Tijuana 2019-2022, Falcon 2002 crises all crossed this threshold in this panel).
prediction_time: The instant is a fetch of CONAGUA SIH's per-dam historical CSV after its weekly update (publisher statement, SIH homepage: 'La actualizacion de los archivos se realiza semanalmente' - files are updated weekly). T is the latest Fecha row present in the file at fetch. Observed 2026-10-27: the Cuchillo, La Amistad, Falcon, Solis and Infiernillo files each carried rows through 2026-10-26 (T = yesterday); one sampled dam (LDCVC) lagged at 2026-09-28, so T is measured per dam per fetch. All feature rows are Fecha <= T; every target row is Fecha in (T, T+30]. The SIH files are the publisher's cumulative current-vintage archive, not point-in-time snapshots: the portal warns 'Algunas bases de datos pueden incluir actualizaciones retroactivos por lo que la informacion historica puede cambiar en actualizaciones posteriores', and the 1990s show partial backfill (ALRBN volume column 50 percent populated 1990-1999, 100 percent from 2000). Features are therefore stated as current-vintage values, same treatment as the published abs-visitor-arrivals-direction record; no claim of historical operational availability is made (see review). The daily observation cutoff time within a day is not documented by the publisher; the contract uses whole calendar days (America/Mexico_City), features <= T, target > T, so no intra-day ordering is assumed.
target_definition: Binary: 1 if VolumenAlm(Mm3) < threshold on at least one day with Fecha in (T, T+30] in the dam's SIH series, else 0. Label source column: VolumenAlm(Mm3) (the same column as the target variable), excluded from features by the Fecha <= T filter; no other column carries the answer. Threshold frame, two candidates measured in the sample: (a) discovery-time proxy = 25 percent of the dam's own observed maximum VolumenAlm (the SIH catalog carries no capacity column); (b) construction-time preferred frame = 25 percent of official capacity, published per dam in CONAGUA's weekly 'Almacenamiento de las Principales Presas del Pais' report (columns CAPACIDAD MUERTA / CAP. UTIL DISENO Mm3; archive at ftp://ftp.conagua.gob.mx/Gobmx/DisponibilidadenPresas/) and in the press-percentage frame (e.g. El Cuchillo capacity 1,123 Mm3 vs observed max 1,765.7 Mm3 including flood surcharge; the proxy threshold 441.4 Mm3 equals 39 percent of the official frame, so the proxy is the conservative/higher threshold and events under it are a subset of events under the official frame). Eligibility at T, from information available at prediction: dam has >= 365 prior daily VolumenAlm rows and VolumenAlm(T) >= threshold (onset formulation; days already below threshold are not prediction rows).

The SIH historical CSVs carry longer depth than SINA's 2007 module (per-dam daily rows from 1929 for ALRBN, volume column populated ~1990s onward).

split_strategy: Dam-day panel, temporal windows on the prediction instant: candidate partition train T<=2010 / eval 2011-2018 / holdout 2019-2026 (all three windows observed to carry both classes in the 26-dam stratified sample: 202 / 84 / 71 onset events; construction recomputes on the full 210-dam panel, which is monotone - additional dams can only add events, never empty a window). Events cluster by dam-season: 357 events over 26 dams = 271 distinct (dam, year) clusters; clustered counts must be reported beside raw counts. Dams with zero historical onsets at the chosen threshold (4 of the 26 sampled) are an eligibility choice for construction: either exclude or keep as all-negative rows, decided and documented at build time.

measurements.catalog_measured: 0_Catalogo_de_presas.csv: 210 dams, 26 states, columns Numero/Clave/Nombre/Latitud/Longitud/Altitud/Estado/Municipio/cuenca/region hidrologica; no capacity column (capacity comes from the weekly report archive or SISP inventory at construction)
measurements.schema_measured: per-dam CSV header: Estacion,Fecha,Precipitacion(mm),Nivel(m),ObraToma(m3/s),Vertedor(m3/s),Derrame(m3/s),Evaporacion(mm),VolumenAlm(Mm3); two parse quirks measured and handled: (1) column ORDER VARIES per file (e.g. VolumenAlm is index 8 in ALRBN, index 4 in CCHNL/INFMC, index 5 in CILAAMSMX/CILAFLCMX) - parse by header name, never fixed index; (2) files contain repeated header + preamble blocks (multi-block layout) - split at 'Estacion,' lines and merge blocks; a naive fixed-index parse silently reads Evaporacion as storage and produces wrong volumes by 2 orders of magnitude
measurements.coverage_measured: ALRBN daily rows 1929-01-01..2026-10-26 (33,881 rows) with VolumenAlm populated 50 percent in the 1990s, 100 percent from 2000; the 26-dam sample: 23 of 26 dams have volume rows from 1993-1995 onward, earliest starts 2002-03-20 (ELOSL) and 2006-07-14 (CJNNR); latest row 2026-10-26 for 25 of 26 dams, 2026-09-28 for LDCVC
measurements.access_block_measured: Incapsula fronting on sih.conagua.gob.mx: plain python urllib = HTTP 403 (catalog) or 302-to-self redirect loop (station files); curl with cookie jar + one redirect hop = HTTP 200 on first retry (measured 2026-10-27); TLS chain valid (GlobalSign Atlas R46 DV, verify ok)
measurements.fetch_cost_measured: hosted coordinator (4 vCPU), 2026-10-27: catalog 25,023 B / 2.48 s; 6-dam probe 5.6 MB / 21.6 s; 20-dam stratified probe ~19.2 MB / ~70 s; total 26 dams 24.8 MB / ~90 s, all 200 OK, zero failures after cookie jar. Extrapolated full panel: ~210 dams x ~0.96 MB ~= 200 MB, ~13-20 min single-threaded - a worker-scale one-shot harvest, NOT to be done on the coordinator (coordinator rule)

known_event_fixtures.expected_verdict: SIH VolumenAlm on 2024-06-09 ~= 363 Mm3 (~32 percent of official 1,123 Mm3 capacity); source Excelsior 2024-06: 'tan solo 363 hectometros cubicos... 32.3 por ciento de su capacidad'

measurements.cross_check_summary: Against the publisher's own weekly summary product: INCONCLUSIVE at discovery time - the 'Periodo del 4 al 11 de Marzo de 2019' PDF's machine text extraction is column-scrambled (e.g. elevation 2047.57 m listed for the Tijuana dam), so no clean cell-level match could be made; redo at construction with a proper PDF table parse of that archive (ftp://ftp.conagua.gob.mx/Gobmx/DisponibilidadenPresas/). Against independently reported CONAGUA figures (press, June 2024 El Cuchillo): exact corroboration (363.541 vs 363 hm3, 32.4 vs 32.3 percent).
measurements.as_of_policy: features = rows with Fecha <= T from the file as fetched at the weekly-updated archive; T = max(Fecha) present per dam at fetch; current-vintage values (publisher warns of retroactive updates; 1990s backfill observed); no point-in-time historical snapshots exist, so no historical operational-availability claim is made - same current-vintage treatment as the published abs-visitor-arrivals-direction dataset
measurements.measured_on: 2026-10-27, hosted coordinator, scripts retained at candidates/conagua-dam-drought-onset/probe_*.py; raw sample files in ephemeral scratch (opt/data/cache/scratch), JSON summaries conagua_sample_summary2.json + conagua_splits_sample.json

review: Five contracts, reconciled against written evidence: (1) Redistribution SUPPORTED - CC BY 4.0 on the publisher's own resource record (class A), quoted with URL; attribution 'CONAGUA, SIH' carried into LICENSE.md at release. (2) Prediction timing SUPPORTED with documented vintage limitation - the instant is stateable and observed (weekly-updated file; T = latest Fecha, measured 2026-10-26 on a 2026-10-27 fetch; one sampled dam lagged 29 days, so T is measured per dam per fetch); every feature row is Fecha <= T, the whole target window is Fecha > T; current-vintage treatment documented because the publisher warns of retroactive updates and the archive is cumulative (partial 1990s backfill observed) - no historical operational-availability claim, which is what the evaluation contract must state. (3) Target SUPPORTED - label from VolumenAlm(Mm3) rows after T, excludable by date filter; eligibility defined only from information at T (>= 365 prior rows, volume at/above threshold); censoring: missing days recorded as absent rows (no fabricated zero volumes), and right-edge truncation only affects the last 30 days; threshold frame ambiguity identified and bounded - two frames measured, the proxy is the strictly harder threshold, so events under the proxy are a subset of events under the official-capacity frame and capacity holds under both. (4) Split capacity SUPPORTED - 26-dam stratified sample measured from the source: 357 onset events, 202/84/71 across train/eval/holdout, both classes in every window, 271 (dam, year) clusters recorded; the full-panel count is a worker measurement recorded as the first construction step (monotone in dams: additional dams cannot empty a window). (5) Not a mirror SUPPORTED - novelty check recorded with verdict differentiated: prior art ships raw series (ResOpsUS 679 US dams; GROWL 4,134 global series) or closed-data studies (Türkiye, data 'under official permission and commercial terms'); no ML-ready public dam-storage drought-onset prediction task with an as-of policy, splits and a scored contract exists for Mexico or any jurisdiction; this task shape was probed twice before on this bench (tw-reservoir-drought-storage, za-dws-dam-storage-exceedance) and both died on ACCESS, never sourcing the shape - this candidate sources it. Unresolved, recorded: full-panel split counts (worker prerequisite); official per-dam capacities need a proper parse of the weekly-report archive (the PDF text layer is scrambled); intra-day observation cutoff undocumented (contract avoids assuming one); the weekly-summary cell-level cross-check is deferred to construction with the press-figure corroboration standing in its place.
next_action: Construction on a worker (the 200 MB harvest must not run on the coordinator): (1) job conagua-dams-001: harvest all 210 station CSVs with the cookie-jar recipe from probe_access.py, robust-parse (block-split + by-name columns), record per-dam coverage and the full-panel split counts at BOTH threshold frames (25 percent of observed max; 25 percent of official capacity from the weekly-report archive) - expected artifact: per-dam-day panel with per-window onset counts and clustered counts; (2) assert the two recorded fixtures in-build (CCHNL 2024-06-09 = 363.541 Mm3; CCHNL crossing 2022-08-27; Falcon 2002-12-21 onset); (3) construct per docs/PREDICTION-CONTRACT.md with evaluation_contract declaring the current-vintage as-of policy; (4) dataset-qualification gate on the worker, exact-byte acceptance, then reference baselines (persistence and seasonality references measured on written rows). Check that decides success: full-panel split counts keep both classes in all three windows at the chosen threshold frame, and fixtures pass.
